claims.gate_note: the id changed from the loose word "kat" to the declared heavy check: the old value named nothing that exists, which is what C3 now refuses

claims.claim: every kernel cell the matrix calls `done` for a vector/DSP tier produces output equal to the scalar row **on the target**, not only on the machine that wrote the body: bit equality for the elementwise and integer cells, a relative window of 4e-06 for the accumulating ones
claims.why_it_was_missing: the tier parity tests under test_package/test/unit are compiled for the target but only run on the host, and the only cross-run path (this KAT) used to compile the scalar sources alone -- so on a target the claim rested on a probe run by hand (gaps G-73)
claims.how: the k3_tier_parity chain compares the scalar row and the tier row in one process; the cell list is generated from src/kernel/matrix.yml for the tier being built, so the chain cannot claim a cell the matrix does not or skip one it does; a cell the matrix calls done that the tier did not register is a failure (exit 12), and so is a run that compared zero elements
claims.verdicts: 7 builds PASS, 62 cell comparisons (arm_neon 11 cells x 4 builds = 44, arm_m 3 x 2 = 6, rvv 12 x 1 = 12; every cell is itself compared over 12 corpus lengths); 5 builds SKIP with their reason printed
claims.red_proof: a wrong NEON body (`vaddq_f32` -> `vsubq_f32`) makes aarch64-linux:base fail with qemu exit 23, and a wrong RVV body (`vfadd` -> `vfsub`) makes rv64-virt:base fail with the same code: 23 is 20 + the index of the `add` cell in the generated table, so the exit code names which cell disagreed; both files were restored and their md5 matched before and after; additionally a wrong NEON dequantize scale and a wrong RVV quantize clamp each make their target fail with 23 = 20 + the cell index

excluded.graph_level_ops: k3 compares kernels only; conv2d/maxpool parity is k2's job and stays there
excluded.saturation_corners: the two quantised dot-product cells run with a clamping AND a non-clamping multiplier so both tiers must saturate alike, but the exact corner values are pinned by the host unit tests, not here

claims.host: zc Linux, QEMU 8.2.2, house arm-toolchain/11.3.rel1 + rv-toolchain/14.3.rel1
claims.reproduce: python3 .github/project/qa/kat/run_kat.py --chain k3  (needs the house cross toolchains and qemu, which the project-gates job does not have)
claims.not_in_ci: the project-gates job has no house cross toolchain and no qemu, so this runs from preflight or by hand; toolchains.json:heavy_checks declares it with that reason
claims.counts_note: the counts were 9/2/10 (50 comparisons) until 2026-11-26, when fc/int8 landed on arm_neon and rvv (G-79) and relu/int8 on arm_m (G-83); the claim gate found the staleness on its first run. They became 11/3/12 (62 comparisons) the same day when `mul` landed (G-94), and this time the gate could not see the change at all -- both sides of the count check derive from `emit_k3_cells.MODES`, so a kernel missing from that map is invisible to it; `census_gate` R11 is the rule that now refuses it. `commit` points at the tree the 62 comparisons were measured on

claims.claim: the same `model.blob` the host gtest reads is also parsed and executed on the target: `k2_conv_micro` runs twice inside one process, once hand-written and once driven by the blob's own node table, and the two agree bit for bit on every QEMU target
claims.why_it_was_missing: the blob carried the graph from G-92 on, but only the host gtest read it; the target chain still spelled the graph out and took only the weights from the generated header, so the evidence stopped exactly between 'the host runs a data-driven graph' and 'the target runs a hand-written one'
claims.how: `.github/project/qa/kat/blob_graph.c` parses the v2 header/node/slot tables and drives the public L2 operators; `emit_blob_image.py` compiles the blob in as raw bytes, not float literals, because `1e-7` round-tripping silently differs between newlib and glibc. Every operator re-derives its own output shape and compares it against the slot's declaration, so a wrong generator is red instead of feeding garbage floats to the next layer
claims.red_proof: two mutations on the real tree, both restored byte-for-byte by md5: `kernel 3->1` in the node table makes the chain fail at the shape re-derivation (exit 10); `act relu->none` leaves a graph whose geometry is entirely valid, so the only thing that can go red is the bitwise comparison itself -- and it does (exit 10)

excluded.numerical_correctness: the in-chain comparison is between two implementations, so it proves equivalence rather than correctness; the values are judged against numpy by the host gtest `graph_blob_k2.cpp`, and the chain's single judgement stays bit equality
excluded.permanent_negative: the C-side negatives live in this record rather than in CI: a deliberately-corrupt build axis would double the KAT image matrix; the permanent negative cases are the C++ executor's `RejectsAMalformedBlob`

claims.claim: a real, pretrained MobileNetV3-Small runs here, on the targets: timm's `mobilenetv3_small_050` (568,224 parameters, 2,270,992 B blob) is exported by torch, imported by `onnx_subset.translate`, and executed from the blob on `m4-an386` and `m7-an500` -- both bit-identical to the host run of the same chain. On the host the worst |difference| against PyTorch is 1.02e-03 on feature values of about 1.6e2 (6e-6 relative), and on the 1000-class head at 96x96 onnxruntime sits between this executor and PyTorch (5.86e-03 vs 2.49e-02), so the residual is float32 accumulation order rather than a defect
claims.why_it_was_missing: until 2026-11-27 the importer had only ever seen the synthetic graph `emit_onnx_blob.py` builds itself, so 'it takes a real model' rested on nothing
claims.how: `export_mobilenet_onnx.py` exports a real pretrained model -- torchvision's `mobilenet_v3_small` for the numerics, timm's `mobilenetv3_small_050` backbone for the target run, because the 1000-class head is 1.0 M of its 2.5 M parameters and no fp32 width fits a 4 MB flash with it (gaps G-109) -- writes the input in blob order (NHWC) and PyTorch's own output as the expectation. The target run is the k2m chain with `INFRINFER_K2M_BLOB` pointing at the imported blob, so the same chain code that runs the synthetic model runs the real one
claims.reproduce: python3 .github/project/qa/prep/export_mobilenet_onnx.py --engine timm --model mobilenetv3_small_050 --num-classes 0 --pretrained --out /tmp/real && python3 .github/project/qa/prep/emit_onnx_blob.py /tmp/real/model.onnx /tmp/real/model.blob && INFRINFER_K2M_BLOB=/tmp/real/model.blob python3 .github/project/qa/kat/run_kat.py --chain k2m

excluded.accuracy: the input is a deterministic ramp, not an image, and no ImageNet claim is made anywhere -- this is a statement about implementations agreeing
excluded.head: the target run uses the backbone without the classifier head; the head is exercised only on the host, where flash is not a constraint

claims.not_in_ci: torch is a machine-level dependency (it authors a model; the repository ships the ONNX and the tensors) and the project-gates job has none of it; Y5 keeps this out of ci.sh by construction

claims.claim: the blob's peak arena scales with the activation area, not with the weights: MobileNetV3-Small imported at 96/80/64/56/48/40/32 gives 105984/73600/47104/36064/26496/20704/11776 arena floats while the blob stays byte-identical at 10,112,128 B. So the input resolution is a memory parameter of the deployment, not a property of the model
claims.why_it_was_missing: the memory table had one row, and the only number in it came from a synthetic network whose gates were constants
claims.how: the same export/import pair at seven resolutions; the arena comes from `blobfmt.plan_arena` over the translated node table, and 96->64 measures 2.25x = (96/64)^2, which is what an arena proportional to activation elements must give
claims.reproduce: for r in 96 80 64 56 48 40 32; do python3 .github/project/qa/prep/export_mobilenet_onnx.py --res $r --out /tmp/sw_$r && python3 .github/project/qa/prep/emit_onnx_blob.py /tmp/sw_$r/model.onnx /tmp/sw_$r/model.blob; done
